question.text: A capacitance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2 </mn><mi>μF</mi></math> is required in an electrical circuit across a potential difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mtext>.</mtext><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kV</mi></math>. A large number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi> </mi><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> capacitors are available which can withstand a potential difference of not more than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The minimum number of capacitors required to achieve this is:

solution.text:
Let us assume that we connect n(whole number) capacitors in series such that the potential difference across the combination is 1000 V. This means the potential difference across each capacitor is

Vcapacitor=1000n V≤300 V

n⩾1000300=3.333.

nmin=4

This means we need to connect at least 4 capacitors in series to make sure that the potential across each one is less than 300 V.

Ceq=mnC=2 μF

m4=2⇒m=8

∴ Minimum no. of capacitors =8×4=32
